name: Manure works beside the Channelsea (F.S. Hempleman & Co., Blood Manure Works & Wharf)
source: Author-supplied london_buildings_1891-96_corr_v1.gpkg (project extract west-ham-buffer-buildings-bng.geojson.gz); cached NLS OS London five-foot 1893; Goad insurance plan London NE vol. F sheet 18, July 1893 (reference/factory-building-survey/goad-f18.tiff)
sourceCRS: EPSG:27700 to scene origin E538900,N183209; x east, z south, metres
method: Manure works 1018 (T19, 4 October 2026): the three legacy OS range envelopes retired; nine records on GeoPackage outlines 1524, 863177 and 944, cut only at Goad F18 compartment walls (similarity-fitted to the outlines), 944 held 6.1 m off the LT&SR centreline; names, uses, storeys, wood/brick and tile roofs read from Goad F18; two Goad chimneys added (one with a printed 40 ft height). Heights in metres are explicit estimates.
evidenceNotes: Goad registration: Goad F18 (reference/factory-building-survey/goad-f18.tiff, July 1893) registered to the GeoPackage outlines by a similarity fit that maximises the overlap of the Goad building colours with fids 1524, 944 and 863177: 0.1594 m per pixel, rotation 20.401 deg, overlap IoU 0.866; GeoPackage vertices lie a median 0.42 m (90th percentile 1.67 m) from the fitted Goad building edge; five hand-read corner controls RMS 2.26 m (max 3.53 m). The fit and its controls are recorded in goadRegistration.
The OS draws both ranges as single shaded blocks with a dashed line and the lettering 'P. Shed' along their railway sides; the GeoPackage outlines include that strip.
Goad prints '(Admission refused)' beside the works: the surveyors did not enter, so compartment uses and figures were read from outside.
